name: Stratus Properties Inc.
business_overview: Stratus Properties Inc., a real estate company, engages in the entitlement, development, management, leasing, and sale of multi and single family residential and commercial real estate properties in the Austin, Texas area, and other select markets in Texas. The company operates through Real Estate Operations and Leasing Operations segments. Its leasing operations cover lease of space at retail and mixed-use and multi-family properties. The company was formerly known as Fm Properties Inc and changed its name to Stratus Properties Inc. in May 1998. Stratus Properties Inc. was incorporated in 1992 and is based in Austin, Texas.

classification_meta.logic_summary: A real estate development and leasing company focused on the Austin, Texas area.

narrative.text:
**Business & market dynamics:** The STRC preferred shares, a key capital-raising vehicle tied to Bitcoin treasury strategy, are trading at a steep discount to par, signaling market skepticism about the sustainability of the dividend and continued Bitcoin purchases. Demand has weakened markedly, pushing the effective yield higher as the instrument slides toward all-time lows. The product’s massive growth from issuance contrasts with the recent exodus of investor confidence, reflecting broader unease with the interplay between crypto exposure and fixed-income commitments in an uncertain macro environment.

**Management strategy and execution:** Leadership, headed by Michael Saylor, has made restoring STRC to par value its foremost operational priority, framing it as the gateway to reigniting the capital engine for future Bitcoin acquisitions. Cantor Fitzgerald analysts who met with Saylor expressed renewed confidence in the plan to stabilize the balance sheet and resume capital raising. The focus now is on execution credibility—whether management can repair market trust in the preferred shares and reestablish the funding pipeline without compromising its Bitcoin-centric vision.

Strategy’s perpetual preferred stock linked to Michael Saylor’s variable-rate Bitcoin yield product, “Stretch” (STRC), slid to near record lows on Tuesday as investors appeared to question whether the company’s latest round of Bitcoin buying can be sustained alongside its dividend commitments.

According to Cointelegraph, STRC fell 3.58% to $91.79 on Tuesday. The move leaves the share price about 8.2% below its $100 target (par) value. Markus Thielen, CEO of 10x Research, said the decline is tied to Strategy’s recent Bitcoin acquisitions, with traders apparently viewing the new purchases as an “unsustainable path” for the preferred offering.

# Strategy’s $10 billion STRC Bitcoin yield product sinks to yearly low as market demands higher payout

CryptoSlate 1 month ago 169

---

---

Strategy’s (formerly MicroStrategy) flagship dividend-paying preferred stock is trading at its weakest level this year, pressuring one of the company’s most important tools for raising capital to buy Bitcoin.

The $10.5 billion variable-rate perpetual preferred stock, which trades under the ticker STRC, closed Tuesday at $91.79.

The settlement marked its third-lowest close since trading began in July 2025 and left the security well below the $100 level that the Michael Saylor-led firm has tried to keep it near.

Over the past year, STRC has expanded from $2.8 billion to $10.5 billion, adding $7.7 billion through at-the-market issuance. This made it one of the fastest-growing financial products in history.

# Strategy’s STRC hit another all-time low today

Protos 3 weeks ago 151

---

---

The market capitalization of Strategy’s STRC, the once-$10.5 billion stock that was supposed to pay better than a high-yield bank account or money market, sank to another all-time low beneath $7.2 billion this morning.

For four uninterrupted days, the stock has crashed lower each day. By 9:33am today, it was trading 29% beneath the par value the company advertises.

Indeed, the price of each STRC share is supposed to trade at $100 while Strategy pays shareholders an 11.5% annualized dividend.

Shares were, in fact, trading at $100 as recently as May 14. Well, this morning, they were trading at $71.25.
